scope: Multi-turn health conversations with physician-written rubrics (7 themes: emergency referrals, context seeking, global health, etc.)
notes: 5,000 conversations, 48,562 rubric criteria written by 262 physicians (60 countries). Conversations mostly synthetically generated by an LLM pipeline, plus physician red-teaming and HealthSearchQA-derived rewrites; users are individual users or health professionals. Variants merged here: HealthBench Hard (1,000) and HealthBench Consensus (3,671). License MIT (simple-evals repo; HF openai/healthbench card). | MEDIC: Open-ended (rubric score); Medmarks: Medmarks-OE, 5,000.

name: HealthBench Hard
title: HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health
scope: Difficult subset of HealthBench conversations
notes: Subset of 1,000 HealthBench examples chosen as difficult for frontier models; merge into healthbench as variant.

name: HealthBench Consensus
title: HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health
scope: HealthBench subset scored only on 34 physician-consensus criteria
notes: Subset of 3,671 HealthBench examples with at least one positive consensus criterion, rubrics filtered to consensus criteria; merge into healthbench as variant.

name: HealthBench Professional
title: HealthBench Professional: Evaluating Large Language Models on Real Clinician Chats
scope: Clinician-facing chat tasks: care consult, writing and documentation, medical research
notes: 525 physician-authored conversations from physicians testing ChatGPT for Clinicians (red-teaming and good-faith), rubric-graded; selected from 15,079 candidates with difficulty-stratified sampling. OpenAI retains a small private held-out set. License not stated in paper; language not stated (examples tagged with a primary language). First author Rebecca Soskin Hicks.

name: First Do NOHARM (NOHARM; MAST uses v2)
title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
scope: Specialist e-consult management plans and harm avoidance across 10 specialties (allergy, cardiology, dermatology, endocrinology, GI, hematology, ID, nephrology, neurology, pulmonology)
notes: MAST: Safety + Management Reasoning dimensions (both MAST General and Clinical composites). PARTIAL ACCESS: 100 base cases + 1,000 physician-perturbed variants = 1,100 items; 30 base cases (330 variants) released open in MAST repo, 70% held out privately for the leaderboard. Cases reconstructed by physicians from real Stanford PCP-to-specialist eConsults (2023-2024); free-text management plan scored by LLM judge vs specialist rubrics. Versions merged: NOHARM v1 (MAST roadmap Dec 2025; arXiv v1 title 'First, do NOHARM: towards clinically safe large language models') and v2 (Mar 2026; used in MAST). Third-party Japanese adaptation of the open subset exists on HF (li-lab/First-do-NOHARM-v2). MAST paper: Goh E et al., 'Toward a test of medical AI superintelligence', Nat Med 32:3128-3130 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04539-8; MAST repo github.com/ARISENetwork/mast; leaderboard arise-ai.org/mast/technical

name: SCT-Bench (Script Concordance Test benchmark; concor.dance)
title: Assessment of Large Language Models in Clinical Reasoning: A Novel Benchmarking Study
scope: Clinical reasoning under uncertainty (diagnostic, investigative, management hypotheses) across medicine, surgery, psychiatry, pediatrics, OB-GYN, emergency medicine, neurology, physiotherapy
notes: MAST: Diagnostic Reasoning (SCT-Diagnostic) + Management Reasoning (SCT-Management). PARTIAL ACCESS: 750 SCT questions from 10 international sources; 174-item open subset (Open Medical SCT + Adelaide SCT) public under MIT; other 8 sources held out for the leaderboard. Items = scenario + hypothesis + new finding; response is a 5-point rating (-2..+2) scored against expert-panel distributions (authors stress 'not multiple choice'). intended_asker coded student because items are medical-education SCT assessment items (judgment). Language of held-out sources not verified (open subset is English). NEJM AI 2(10), 2025; a medRxiv preprint ('Do Language Models Think Like Doctors?', 10.1101/2025.02.11.25321822) appears in search results but was not fetched. MAST paper: Goh E et al., 'Toward a test of medical AI superintelligence', Nat Med 32:3128-3130 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04539-8; MAST repo github.com/ARISENetwork/mast; leaderboard arise-ai.org/mast/technical | [merged from sct_public (SCT-Public (Script Concordance Test))] Medmarks: Medmarks-V SCTPublic, 750. 750 SCT items from 10 international datasets (per search summary). Likely the same as the MAST 'SCT' component - dedupe with MAST fork row. Link between SCT-Public and this medRxiv preprint taken from search results (Medmarks cites McCoy et al., 2025); data URL/licence not verified.

name: CPC-Bench
title: Teaching large language models to reason like expert diagnosticians
scope: Expert diagnostic reasoning on NEJM clinicopathological conferences: differential diagnosis, testing/management plan, literature search, QA, diagnostic touchpoints, information omission, plus image tasks
notes: MAST: Diagnostic Reasoning (CPC DDx, QA) + Management Reasoning (CPC management). 7,102 NEJM CPCs (1923-2025) and 1,021 Image Challenges; 47,648 questions across 10 tasks (7 text-based, 3 multimodal: Image Challenge, VQA, visual DDx) - text-only tasks form a usable text subset. Cases licensed from NEJM; leaderboard set is private (submission via registration at cpcbench.com/submit.html); paper states a public set of 100 modern cases (4,735 questions) will be released upon publication - release not verified. arXiv v1 title: 'Advancing medical artificial intelligence using a century of cases' (cited under that title in the MAST supplement). intended_asker=clinician is a judgment (case-conference presentations). MAST paper: Goh E et al., 'Toward a test of medical AI superintelligence', Nat Med 32:3128-3130 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04539-8; MAST repo github.com/ARISENetwork/mast; leaderboard arise-ai.org/mast/technical

name: MedAgentBench v2
title: MedAgentBench v2: Improving Medical LLM Agent Design
scope: LLM agent tasks in a FHIR-compliant virtual EHR (patient data lookup, conditional logic, ordering medications/labs)
notes: MAST: Agentic Task Completion (radar only; not in MAST composites). v2 adds 300 new multi-step tasks (10 task types x 30 patient variations; generated with o3 from two patients' EHRs, physician-reviewed) to the original MedAgentBench (Jiang Y et al., NEJM AI 2025, doi:10.1056/AIdbp2500144; 300 physician-written tasks, 100 patients). AMBIGUOUS: MAST demo page describes '300 physician-written tasks, 100 Stanford patients, published in NEJM AI' (i.e. v1 task set) while repo README points to test_data_v2.json - which task set MAST scores is unclear; merge with any medagentbench (v1) row. Repo has no license file; PSB paper is CC BY-NC 4.0. MAST paper: Goh E et al., 'Toward a test of medical AI superintelligence', Nat Med 32:3128-3130 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04539-8; MAST repo github.com/ARISENetwork/mast; leaderboard arise-ai.org/mast/technical | Medmarks: Medmarks-OE, 600 agentic FHIR tasks.

name: PhysicianBench
title: PhysicianBench: Evaluating LLM Agents in Real-World EHR Environments
license: Apache-2.0 (tasks/harness); Stanford University Research Data Use Agreement (EHR data)
scope: Long-horizon physician EHR workflows (data retrieval, diagnosis interpretation, prescribing, treatment planning, documentation) across 21 specialties
notes: MAST: Agentic Task Completion (radar only; not in MAST composites). 100 tasks adapted from real PCP-subspecialty e-consults, 670 execution-verified checkpoints, mean 27 tool calls/task; FHIR server with de-identified STARR patient records. Task definitions open on GitHub; EHR Docker image via controlled request-and-approval on Redivis under Stanford DUA. MAST paper: Goh E et al., 'Toward a test of medical AI superintelligence', Nat Med 32:3128-3130 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04539-8; MAST repo github.com/ARISENetwork/mast; leaderboard arise-ai.org/mast/technical

name: ReXrank Mini (subset of ReXrank)
title: ReXrank: A Public Leaderboard for AI-Powered Radiology Report Generation
scope: Chest X-ray radiology report generation (findings and impression) from images
notes: MAST: Radiology dimension (MAST General composite only). ReXrank Mini is MAST's curated subset of ReXrank run on the 3 public test sets (IU X-Ray, MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus), images only with no clinical context, scored with GREEN; full ReXrank adds the private ReXGradient 10,000-study test set. Subset size not published; access varies by source dataset (not verified here). MAST text also mentions VQA for ReXrank Mini but demo shows only report generation. MAST paper: Goh E et al., 'Toward a test of medical AI superintelligence', Nat Med 32:3128-3130 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04539-8; MAST repo github.com/ARISENetwork/mast; leaderboard arise-ai.org/mast/technical

name: Diverse Dermatology Images (DDI)
title: Disparities in dermatology AI performance on a diverse, curated clinical image set
license: Stanford DDI Research Use Agreement (non-commercial research only)
scope: Biopsy-proven skin lesion images across Fitzpatrick skin types (benign vs malignant assessment)
notes: MAST: Medical Images dimension ('Multimodal Images'/'Multimodal Derm', MAST General composite only), combined with MRA-MIDAS. 656 images from 570 patients (Stanford clinics 2010-2020). Image classification dataset; MAST's prompt/instruction wrapping not published. MAST paper: Goh E et al., 'Toward a test of medical AI superintelligence', Nat Med 32:3128-3130 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04539-8; MAST repo github.com/ARISENetwork/mast; leaderboard arise-ai.org/mast/technical

name: MRA-MIDAS (Multimodal Image Dataset for AI-based Skin Cancer)
title: Multimodal Image Dataset for AI-Based Skin Cancer (MIDAS) Benchmarking
scope: Prospectively collected, biopsy-confirmed skin lesions with paired clinical and dermoscopic images and clinical metadata
notes: MAST: Medical Images dimension ('Multimodal Images', MAST General composite only), combined with DDI. Hosted via Stanford AIMI / Redivis (dataset DOI 10.71718/15nz-jv40); public release covers consenting Stanford-site patients; access terms and item count not verified. NEJM AI 2(6), 2025. MAST paper: Goh E et al., 'Toward a test of medical AI superintelligence', Nat Med 32:3128-3130 (2026), doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04539-8; MAST repo github.com/ARISENetwork/mast; leaderboard arise-ai.org/mast/technical
